subject: maths
question: Two trains are travelling towards each other on parallel tracks, 9660 kilometres apart. Train A initially travels at 80 km/hr, and Train B initially travels at 60 km/hr. If Train A's speed is reduced by 10% and Train B's speed is increased by 10%, what is the ratio of the time taken for the trains to meet initially to the time taken after their speed adjustments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time ∝ 1 / (relative speed)

Initial relative speed = 80 + 60 = 140

New speeds ⇒ A = 80 × 0.9 = 72, B = 60 × 1.1 = 66

New relative speed = 72 + 66 = 138

Ratio of time = inverse of speed ratio

= 138 : 140 = 69 : 70

**∴ Answer = 69 : 70**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance same in both cases

Initial speeds: 80 km/hr and 60 km/hr

After change: 72 km/hr and 66 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Initial relative speed = 80 + 60 = 140

⇒ New relative speed = 72 + 66 = 138

⇒ Time ratio = (D/140) : (D/138)

⇒ = 138 : 140

⇒ = 69 : 70

**∴ The correct answer is 69 : 70.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Opposite direction ⇒ speeds add

Time-Speed Relation

For same distance, time ∝ 1/speed

Percentage Change

Decrease 10% ⇒ ×0.9, Increase 10% ⇒ ×1.1

Quick Tip

Use inverse ratio for time comparison
